clue.text: Creativity of that bloke is shown in pastry

indicators.note: something shown in a display sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: tarts are pastry dishes
HE is the pronoun for that bloke

explanation.surface: A man's artistic flair is displayed in his baking.
explanation.definitionFit: The arts are the creative disciplines collectively, so the phrase stands for creativity as a field.

clue.text: Ability to get an old coin

definitions.meaning: a weight and coin of the ancient world, as in the biblical parable

explanation.surface: Someone's skill earns them an antique piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent means natural gift, and separately names an ancient unit of money and weight.

clue.text: Be back before Crosby's decline

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the singer's name
back says the word be is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the American crooner; the 's is the verb 'is' linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Be back before the old crooner starts to fade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing is the falling away of a tide, used as a noun for any decline or waning.

clue.text: What Jesus did for breakfast?

parts.note: read as 'got up on the first morning of the week': Jesus rose on Sunday; the phrase names a Sunday in Lent

explanation.surface: A light question about Jesus's morning routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Breakfast is when you get up; Jesus got up from the dead on a Sunday. The answer is the fourth Sunday of Lent, when rose-coloured vestments are worn.
explanation.definitionFit: The wording describes the Resurrection, rising on the first day, which the church calendar name echoes.

clue.text: Spice up writer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus was the French writer of The Outsider

explanation.surface: An instruction to make an author's prose more lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice up' looks like one verb phrase; 'Spice' is the definition and 'up' turns CAMUS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a tangy dried red berry powder used as a seasoning in Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Dove in America perched eyes down, primarily to take a breather …

indicators.note: to take means the outer letters swallow the other piece
primarily picks the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: a lung is an organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: An American bird sits on a perch, looking down, and pauses for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading letters PED take in LUNG. In American English the past tense of dive is dove.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunged means dived in; Americans say dove where Britons say dived.

clue.text: After sporting event, kisses for high jumpers

indicators.note: after puts the event first, followed by the kisses

parts.note: polo is a sport played on horseback
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Following a match, athletes in the high jump are kissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high jumpers' looks like athletes, but 'jumper' is British for a sweater: these are high-collared sweaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo necks are sweaters with tall folded collars, so jumpers with high necks.

clue.text: One's continually upset to some extent

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset says the letters are turned up, read backwards
to some extent means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone is constantly a bit troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: TINU sits inside 'continually'; 'upset' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one in counting.

clue.text: Adults can be wrong on purpose? Nothing odd in that

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters may be rearranged into something else
nothing odd means the odd-placed letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Is it deliberate when grown-ups err? There's nothing strange about that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' makes GROWN from WRONG; keeping the even letters of 'purpose' gives UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups is the informal word for adults, especially as children see them.

clue.text: Labour's end pitch

definitions.meaning: labour in the sense of childbirth ends with the ... of the baby
a pitch, a thrown ball, is a ... in cricket or baseball; also a sales pitch's ...

explanation.surface: A political-sounding phrase about the Labour Party's final pitch for votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Childbirth ends in the delivery; a bowled or thrown ball is also called a delivery.

clue.text: … parts of which being low, best left incomplete

indicators.note: left incomplete means each word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: some parts of a lung are low, the best left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the breather (LUNG) in 5 across: 'which' is the lung. LOW and BEST each drop their ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Lungs are divided into sections called lobes, so lobes are parts of the breather.

clue.text: Love to follow dictator hiding in Scottish island? It's handy!

indicators.note: hiding in means the other pieces are concealed within the island

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: to follow puts love after the dictator

parts.note: Tito was the dictator of Yugoslavia
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A tyrant has fled to a Hebridean island, followed by his lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's handy!' is a cryptic nod to a tool held in the hand; Mull is a real island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A multitool is a pocket gadget combining many implements, literally convenient to hand.

clue.text: Does cannon shot flash?

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether a fired gun gives off a burst of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is the anagram signal, not the firing of the cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, and 'in a flash' means an instant.

clue.text: Front view partially screened

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking from the front, part of the view is obscured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something screened is broadcast, shown on television.

clue.text: Pleasant folk found in Provence?

definitions.meaning: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Friendly locals live in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means agreeable folk, and read with a capital it means inhabitants of the city of Nice.

clue.text: Groomer getting fix by the Cutty Sark?

indicators.note: by sets the second piece beside the first

parts.note: to nail is to fix in place
the Cutty Sark is a preserved tea clipper, a fast sailing ship, at Greenwich in London

explanation.surface: A stable groom gets repairs done beside a famous old sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail clippers trim fingernails, a grooming tool, so the item grooms.

clue.text: Where spiders might be up against it?

definitions.text: Where spiders might be up against it?

parts.words: Where spiders might be up against it?
parts.note: spiders spin webs in the angle of a room, and the idiom for being trapped with no way out is the same phrase

explanation.surface: Where a spider might find itself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means trapped in a difficult position; literally it is where spiders lurk.

clue.text: Difficult objections raised and delivered

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised says the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'
a baby delivered has been born

explanation.surface: Awkward complaints were raised and then dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person is obstinate and hard to deal with.

clue.text: Slow movers ultimately suffer in misusing dope and LSD

indicators.note: in says one piece is put inside the other
misusing means the letters are mixed up
ultimately picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Drug users end up suffering, those who are slow to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misusing' rearranges the drug words into PLODDES, which then takes the final letter of 'suffer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plodders walk heavily and slowly, or work steadily without flair.

clue.text: Treat all these as a capital

indicators.note: to treat is to process or work on, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to regard every item as a capital letter or asset.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the capital city of the US state of Florida.

clue.text: Like hotel stuff in place of seclusion

parts.note: as means like
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Hotel-style things in a quiet retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat or hermitage, away from the world.

clue.text: See back covered in adhesive plaster

indicators.note: covered in means the piece sits inside the adhesive

parts.note: gum is a glue

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to spy is to see

explanation.surface: Look at someone's back stuck with sticky tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SPY into YPS. 'adhesive plaster' looks like a sticking plaster; 'plaster' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is the mineral from which plaster of Paris is made.

clue.text: Bad typos scattered around the back of newspaper, some of which are here

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the other piece
scattered means the letters are thrown about
the back of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Errors are strewn about the last page of a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points at the clue itself: 'back' is in it, and a back is one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'back' in the clue is one of the body's parts, so they are present here.

clue.text: Parties veto motion by broadcaster and writer

indicators.note: by puts the broadcaster beside what comes before

parts.note: dos are parties

indicators.note: motion means the letters move about

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcaster

explanation.surface: Political parties block a proposal from a TV company and an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veto motion' reads as a vote; 'motion' rearranges VETO into TOEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Fyodor Dostoevsky was the Russian novelist who wrote Crime and Punishment.

clue.text: Make adjustments to the bottom of chainsaw when cutting wood

indicators.note: a piece cutting into another goes inside it

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Fine-tune the base of a power saw while felling timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make small adjustments to something.

clue.text: Colette's soldiers

definitions.meaning: A novella by the French writer Colette

explanation.surface: The troops belonging to the French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is Colette's famous story, and it splits into two GIs, American servicemen.

clue.text: Naughty niece after honour at last redeemed for good behaviour

indicators.note: after puts the niece's letters behind the rest

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word
naughty signals the letters misbehave and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly behaved niece, finally reformed after receiving an award, is rewarded for good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is doing as one is told, the conduct of a well-behaved person.

clue.text: See 21
Naming and shaming starts and row gets worse

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letters of the words

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Public shaming begins and the quarrel gets uglier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is more unpleasant, so worse in comparison.

clue.text: Just get rid of dad but don't let on!

definitions.meaning: dispose of father only, so keep the mother

explanation.surface: Advice to dispose of a father and stay quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep mum is an idiom for staying silent; literally it is retaining your mother.
